key_provisions_or_claims: Medical devices must meet Annex I essential requirements before being placed on the market.
Devices are classified into Classes I, IIa, IIb and III under Annex IX, with conformity procedures scaled to risk.
Notified bodies assess conformity; compliant devices bear the CE marking.
Manufacturers and Member States must report incidents, malfunctions and recalls through a vigilance system.
Clinical investigations are notified to authorities and need ethics committee opinions; harmonized standards give presumption of conformity.
annotation.summary_en: Council Directive 93/42/EEC harmonizes EU rules on medical devices: essential safety and performance requirements, four risk classes, notified-body conformity assessment, CE marking, vigilance reporting and clinical investigation rules. It does not mention robots or AI; it is relevant only as a baseline for physical medical devices, including software. It was later repealed by Regulation (EU) 2017/745.
